input.quote: 19.2 For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.
input.rationale: Sections 19.1, 19.3 and 19.4 are adequate: professional and workmanlike services, conformity to documentation, no malicious code, compliance with Applicable Law, and a repair/re-perform/replace-then-refund remedy, with 19.5 expressly preserving express warranties from the disclaimer. The material failure is duration: Section 19.2 caps the Deliverable conformity warranty at fifteen days after delivery and then extinguishes any correction or refund obligation, which also cuts off the 19.1 conformity warranty in practice. Fifteen days is below the fallback of 90 days for software and 30 days for services, and it expires at essentially the same time as the fifteen-business-day acceptance window in Section 6.1, leaving no post-acceptance protection. We propose 90 days with the Section 19.4 remedy preserved for nonconformities reported during the period.

proposal.summary: Extend Deliverable conformity warranty from 15 to 90 days and preserve the Section 19.4 remedy
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Deliverable conformity warranty from fifteen to ninety days and removed the blanket cut-off of correction and refund obligations, so the Section 19.4 repair/replace/refund remedy remains available for nonconformities we report during the warranty period. Our playbook position is 90 days for deliverables and software with a real remedy; a 15-day period expiring at the same time as acceptance testing gives us no practical protection.

ops.oldText: For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.
ops.newText: For ninety (90) days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation. Vendor's obligations under Section 19.4 apply to any nonconformity Customer reports during that period.
